text:
ops-bot: Heads-up: Regional instance pool eu-west1 will undergo a short rolling eviction tonight 23:30-00:30 UTC for kernel/security updates. No API schema changes.

maya: copying this here — is there any expected customer-visible downtime or degraded tail latency?

jordan: We expect transient 95p latency spikes for tails on large-context workloads during the node restart window. No full outage expected thanks to draining.

raj: Procedure summary on-call should follow: 1) start drain on target nodes, 2) verify request routing off node, 3) restart, 4) validate KV cache warm.

maya: can you paste the drain command used in prod?

jordan: Sure — use this snippet onctl: 
```
# drain node example
./onctl nodes drain --region eu-west1 --pool infer-pool-4 --timeout 300
```

liz: From CS side: we'll push a proactive blurb to customers with heavy reserved capacity. Need copy approved before 21:00 UTC.

maya: Will any Dedicated customers be impacted beyond soft latency bumps? I want to confirm SLA exposure.

raj: Dedicated reserved pools are isolated; only a small subset of shared spillover traffic may see reroutes. SLA hit unlikely but flagging for post-window review.

ops-bot: AUTO: incident-mode set to maintenance, alert routing -> eng-oncall, pager escalation window extended by +30m.

maya: Ok, plan: Jordan runs a single-node test at 22:30 on a canary subset, reports metrics to thread. If good, proceed 23:30 rolling. Raj you’re primary for pager for escalations. Liz will send customer note.

jordan: Acknowledged. I'll run canary and drop perf numbers here.

liz: Draft customer blurb: "We will perform a short maintenance in eu-west1 on <date> 23:30–00:30 UTC. You may see brief latency increases for requests routed through eu-west1; no data access interruption expected. Reach support@redwood.ai for concerns." OK to send?

maya: Tweak to include link to status page and contact for Dedicated support. After that, send.

raj: If the canary shows >20% 95p latency increase we pause and roll back; otherwise continue. I'll standby.

ops-bot: Reminder: please add runbook step IDs to thread when you act: RB-evac-13, RB-node-restart-2.

jordan: Canary started 22:30 — initial 95p 180ms -> 210ms, CPU fine, no errors. Pushing results to metrics dashboard: https://telemetry.redwood.ai/d/evac/ew1-canary

maya: Looks within expected envelope. Proceed with rolling sequence at 23:30. Update here when each node finishes.

jordan: Node 1/6 drained and restarted — no errors. Node 2/6 drain in progress.

raj: Acknowledge. If any customer pings, escalate to me and I’ll coordinate rollback.

liz: Customer notice scheduled for 21:05 UTC with status page link + dedicated contact.

jordan: All nodes done 00:18 UTC. KV cache warm verified, 95p back to baseline.

maya: Thanks team. Closing maintenance. Please add postmortem note if any unexpected follow-ups: tag RB-evac-post and customer impact summary.

ops-bot: AUTO: maintenance completed, incident-mode cleared, summary task created RB-evac-post-1749123456.

liz: Sent final customer follow-up with completion timestamp.

maya: Great work.
